Re:    Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC
       Texas Gateway Project
       Docket No. CP26-547-000
       Minor Workspace/Alignment Updates and Environmental Correspondence

Dear Ms. Reese:

       On June 26, 2026, Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC (“Gulf South”) submitted an
Abbreviated Application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity Authorization for
the Texas Gateway Project (“Project”) in the subject docket. Since the filing of the application,
Gulf South has incorporated certain modifications to the proposed Project to reduce environmental
impacts, address constructability issues, and accommodate landowner requests.

Minor Workspace/Alignment Updates
       Gulf South has prepared this supplemental filing to provide the Federal Energy Regulatory
Commission (“Commission” or “FERC”) with updated information relating to minor reroutes of
the Project’s mainline pipeline, minor changes to and minor workspace modifications that have
occurred subsequent to the June 26, 2026 certificate application filing. The pipeline re-routes and
modifications reflected in the supplemental filing materials have resulted in a minor net increase
in construction-related impacts by approximately 63.52 acres (2.14%) and a net increase in
operation-related impacts by approximately 3.90 acres (0.39%).

Landowner Updates
        The minor alignment and workspace updates will impact two additional landowners. Gulf
South is in active negotiations with these landowners to acquire the necessary easements for the
Project, and has sent these landowners the required landowner notification package pursuant to 18
C.F.R. § 157.6(d). In addition, Gulf South notes that it continues to be actively engaged with its
landowners and has acquired tracts for approximately 50% of the landowners.

Environmental
       The updated information also includes recent environmental correspondence not
previously submitted capturing continued agency coordination. Gulf South is also providing
updated alignment sheets, construction drawings, and plans, including geotechnical investigations
completed since the filing of the application.

 Supplemental Filing Summary
       On June 26, 2026, Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC (Gulf South) filed an application
with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC or the Commission) pursuant to
Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act and Part 157 of the Commission’s regulations, seeking
authorization for construction and operation of the Texas Gateway Project (Project; Docket No.
CP26-547-000). Since the filing of the application, Gulf South has incorporated certain minor
modifications to the proposed Project to reduce environmental impacts, address constructability
issues, and accommodate landowner requests.

       The purpose of this filing is to provide an overview of the proposed workspace and
alignment modifications and to provide FERC with updated information regarding the associated
impacts on the relevant resources discussed in Resource Reports 1 through 12 submitted as part
of the application. This filing also provides the results of the geotechnical investigations that have
been completed to date and documentation of agency correspondence not previously filed.

       In total, Gulf South has incorporated 41 modifications to the proposed Project. These
modifications have resulted in a net increase in construction-related impacts by approximately
63.52 acres (2.14 %) and a net increase in operation-related impacts by approximately 3.90 acres
(0.39 %). Detailed descriptions of the proposed modifications are provided in Table 1 below.

 RESOURCE REPORT 1
Section 1.1            Project Description

       Gulf South is filing an Application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
with FERC for authorization to construct, own, operate, and maintain new greenfield facilities and
modified and/or expanded existing facilities. Specifically, Gulf South is proposing to construct a
new approximately 155-mile-long natural gas pipeline comprised of 36-inch- and 42-inch-
diameter pipe segments (herein referred to as the Texas Gateway Pipeline), three new delivery
meter and regulator (M&R) stations, and other appurtenant facilities in east Texas and southwest
Louisiana.    Gulf South also proposes to construct a new 13,410 nominal horsepower1 (hp)
compressor station (herein referred to as the Cleveland Compressor Station [CS]) along its
existing Index 129 Legacy System in San Jacinto County, Texas. Further, Gulf South proposes
to expand its existing Carthage Junction CS and Magasco CS by installing additional compressor
units capable of adding an additional 39,260 nominal hp2 and 44,961 nominal hp3 at the respective
stations and a new bi-directional check M&R station at the Carthage Junction CS. Overall, the
Project will allow Gulf South to transport approximately 1.8 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas
from existing facilities in Carthage, Texas to delivery points in southeast Texas and southwest
Louisiana.

Section 1.3.6          Construction Schedule

       To meet market demand, Gulf South’s planned in-service date for Project facilities is as
early as December 2028.         Pending all necessary authorizations and permits, Gulf South
anticipates mobilization and construction to start as early as 1st Quarter 2028. This schedule is
based on the Gulf South’s request for final approval by the FERC no later than December 2027
as well as the anticipated receipt of permits and approvals (see Section 1.6).

Section 2.2.2         Springs

       Based on field surveys conducted within the Project area and a review of the U.S.
Geological Survey (USGS) National Water Information System tool, there is potentially one spring
located within one mile of temporary access road (TAR) TAR-033 (2,364 feet west) (USGS,
2026a) but is not crossed or otherwise impacted by the Project.

Section 2.2.3         Sole-source Aquifers and Wellhead Protection Areas

       Information obtained from the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality and Texas
Commission on Environmental Quality confirmed there are nine wellhead protection areas within
1 mile of the Project workspace (Ables, 2026; Molieri, 2026).

Section 2.2.4         Public and Private Water Supply Wells

       Public and private water supply wells located within the vicinity of the Project were
identified through a review of data provided by Louisiana Department of Conservation and Energy
(LDCE) and the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) (LDCE, 2026; TWDB, 2026).

Section 2.3.1         Waterbodies Crossed or Otherwise Impacted by the Project Facilities

       Gulf South has identified 766 waterbody crossings within the Project area. Of these, 331
were identified as ephemeral streams,113 as perennial streams, 274 as intermittent streams, and
48 as ponds. Of the 766 waterbody crossings, 9 are classified as major waterbodies.

Section 2.3.3         Public Watershed Areas

       The Texas Gateway Pipeline and associated aboveground facilities are located within 40
hydrologic unit code 12 watersheds, as presented in Appendix 2E.

Section 2.3.4         Floodplains

       Zone A is crossed by 15.36 miles of the Project, while Zone AE (including the floodway)
is crossed by 2.85 miles of the Project. Zone X (shaded) is crossed by 0.96 mile of the Project
(Federal Emergency Management Agency [FEMA], 2026).

Section 2.3.6         Sensitive Surface Waters

       There is one river identified as both a Section 10 (i.e., navigable) water as well as listed
on the National Park Service (NPS) Nationwide Rivers Inventory (the Sabine River) that is crossed



                                               11
 by the Project at milepost (MP) 120.38 (NPS, 2026a; U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, 2024, 2011);
however, direct impacts to the Sabine River will be avoided utilizing the horizontal directional drill
(HDD) crossing method.

       The Project crosses one Ecologically Significant Stream Segment (the Sabine River) at
MP 120.38 (Texas Parks and Wildlife Department [TPWD], 2008).

       The Project will cross the scenic river of Beckwith Creek at MP 136.24 and MP 136.30,
and Hickory Branch at MP 147.05 and MP 147.22 in Beauregard Parish, Louisiana (Louisiana
Department of Wildlife and Fisheries [LDWF], 2026a, 2026b). Gulf South will submit a Scenic
Rivers Permit Application to the LDWF for both of the above waterbody crossings in 1st Quarter
of 2028.

Section 2.4.1          Existing Wetland Resources

       A total of 930 wetlands were identified within the Project area during field survey and
desktop analysis, conducted from November 2025 through August 2026.


RESOURCE REPORT 3
Section 3.1            Introduction

       Habitat assessments were conducted from November 2025 through August 2026.

Section 3.2.1          Fishery Classification

       Gulf South has identified 766 waterbody crossings within the Project area. Of these, 113
were identified as perennial streams, 274 as intermittent streams, 331 as ephemeral streams,
and 48 as manmade or natural ponds.

Section 3.2.2          Fisheries of Special Concern

       Sam Rayburn Reservoir is within 0.25 mile of the Project from MP 75.25 to MP 75.51, with
the nearest public access facility (Mill Creek Park) 2.28 miles from MP 77.22.             However,
Highway 96 and an existing utility corridor run parallel with this stretch of the proposed pipeline
and are located between the Project and the reservoir. No other designated recreational or
commercial fisheries are located within the Project area, nor will any be otherwise impacted by
the Project (LDWF, 2026a; TPWD, 2026)

       Waterbodies with fisheries of special concern include those that support fisheries of
exceptional recreational value, such as trout populations; those that provide habitat for a protected


                                                 12
 species; or those that are assigned a special state fishery management designation. State and
federal agencies may regulate these waterbodies by imposing timing restrictions for in-stream
activities and/or specialized construction techniques. However, LDWF reviewed the Project and
provided state agency approval allowing instream work outside of June 1 through November 30
in the event it is required by the Project (Chain, 2026). TPWD’s review of the Project is underway
and approval will be filed with FERC upon receipt (Bronson-Warren, 2026).

Section 3.3.3          Protected and Sensitive Areas

        The Project crosses a portion of Sabine National Forest in Sabine County, Texas, totaling
2.82 miles of land owned in fee by the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) (USFS, 2026a). The Moore
Plantation WMA falls within this portion of the Sabine National Forest and is crossed by the Project
for 2.44 miles. Further information on public lands crossed by the Project, including MP ranges
and proposed crossing methods, is provided in Table 8.4-1 of Resource Report 8. Additionally,
the Project workspace is within 0.25 mile of the Sabine National Forest from MP 41.79 to
MP 42.66, with the closest distance (0.08 mile) occurring at MP 42.40.


RESOURCE REPORT 4
4.2.1   Project Area of Potential Effect

        The Project Area of Potential Effect (APE) for direct effects totals 3,053 acres. The APE
for indirect effects was considered to be the geographic area from which any permanent
aboveground facility has the potential to diminish or alter the setting of a National Register of
Historic Places (NRHP)-listed or NRHP-eligible property.

4.2.3   Survey Methods

        The cultural resources investigations for the Project were conducted in accordance with
the Texas Historical Commission (THC) and Louisiana Division of Archeology (LDOA) survey
standards, as well as approved scopes of work. Additionally, as portions of the Project traverse
federal lands, the Phase I surveys were also conducted in accordance with Archaeological
Resource Protection Act (ARPA) Permit Number SAB26101 issued by the USFS.

4.2.4   Summary of Field Investigations

        The results of cultural resources investigations presented herein were conducted from
November 10, 2025 to August 12, 2026 and represent 100 percent of the total Project footprint.


                                                13
 These investigations included an excavation of a total of 15,105 shovel tests, 116 augers, and 19
mechanically excavated trenches. These efforts resulted in the revisit or documentation of 27
newly recorded cultural resources, and the revisit of 5 previously recorded sites within the Project
Environmental Survey Area. Of these, a total of 12 archeological sites possess sufficient research
value, integrity, or historic significance to be considered eligible for listing in the NRHP. Gulf
South has designed their workspace (i.e., APE) to ensure no Project impacts occur to these
resources, or contributing components thereof via the implementation of construction-based
avoidance methods such as reroutes, HDDs, and/or 50.0-foot (15.2-meter) avoidance buffers.
Additionally, Gulf South will install exclusionary fencing along the boundary of workspace within
the vicinity of eligible sites to ensure no inadvertent trespassing occurs at these locations.

4.3.1   U.S. Forest Service

        In accordance with 18 CFR §§ 380.12(f) and 380.14, and in support of FERC’s obligations
to consult under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA), Gulf South
submitted an ARPA permit application to the USFS on March 12, 2026. The ARPA Permit
(No. SAB926101) was issued on June 30, 2026. The results of the surveys across federal lands
were detailed in a stand-alone report and submitted to the USFS on August 17, 2026. In
correspondence dated September 1, 2026, the USFS provided comments to the draft report and
requested revisions. The revised draft report will be submitted to the USFS in the 4th Quarter of
2026. Gulf South will file records of any future correspondence with the USFS with FERC upon
receipt.

4.3.2   Texas Historical Commission

        In accordance with 18 CFR §§ 380.12(f) and 380.14, and in support of FERC’s obligations
to consult under Section 106 of the NHPA, Gulf South submitted the Phase I Report to the THC
for review and comment on June 26, 2026. In correspondence dated August 6, 2026, the THC
requested revisions to the draft report. The revised draft report will be submitted to the THC in
the 4th Quarter of 2026. Gulf South will file records of any future correspondence with the THC
with FERC upon receipt.

4.3.3   Louisiana Division of Archeology

        In accordance with 18 CFR §§ 380.12(f) and 380.14, and in support of FERC’s obligations
to consult under Section 106 of the NHPA, Gulf South submitted the Phase I Report to the LDOA



                                                 14
 for review and comment on June 26, 2026. Gulf South requested concurrence that the proposed
Project activities presented to date will have no effect on historic properties. In correspondence
dated August 19, 2026, the LDOA provided a determination that the Project would have no effect
to historic properties. The LDOA also requested editorial revisions to the draft report. The revised
Final report will be submitted to the LDOA in the 4th Quarter of 2026. Gulf South will file records
of any future correspondence with the LDOA with FERC upon receipt.

Section 5.2.5           Localized Environmental and Socioeconomic Impact

        As further detailed in Appendix 5A, the Project will impact a total of 63 census block
groups, and of these, 35 census block groups (56 percent) are considered sensitive and
vulnerable communities based on the percentage of households below the poverty level and/or
the population represented by minorities.

Section 5.2.6           Limited English-Speaking Households

        Of the census block groups either directly impacted by Project activities or within the
respective localized environmental and socioeconomic impact review areas to each aboveground
facility, there are approximately 28,684 households.


RESOURCE REPORT 6
Section 6.3             Blasting

        The total area underlain by shallow bedrock is approximately 329.52 acres (approximately
11 percent of the total Project area); however, no blasting is anticipated to be required for the
Project.

Section 6.4             Mineral Resources

        There are 299 oil and gas wells identified within 0.25 mile of the Project (LDCE, 2026;
Railroad Commission of Texas, 2026).

        As summarized in Table 6.4-1 below, there are a total of 15 gravel pits and 3 clay pits
within 1 mile of the Project (USGS, 2026b). Of these, one gravel pit occurs within the Project
workspaces associated with TAR-087. However, this pit appears to be historic as recent satellite
imagery indicates that the area is currently being utilized for silviculture activities.




                                                   15
 Section 6.5.1           Seismic Hazards

          According to the USGS Seismic Hazards maps for the U.S., the Project is situated in areas
of low seismic probability. Based on historical seismic activity in the area, the USGS estimates
that the 500 year earthquake (an earthquake with a 10 percent probability of occurring within any
50-year interval) would result in peak ground accelerations between 1 to 3 percent gravity
(USGS, 2018). Additionally, the USGS estimates that the peak ground accelerations with a 2
percent probability of exceedance in 50 years would be 4 to 10 percent gravity (USGS, 2018).
Peak ground accelerations between 0 and 4 percent gravity are associated with the lightest
ground motions with no potential for damage. Peak ground accelerations between 4 and 10
percent gravity are associated with moderate to strong ground motions, but a very light to light
potential for damage (Wald et al., 1999; USGS, 2026c). Therefore, if an earthquake were to occur
in the Project area, the likelihood that it would result in significant damage to the Project facilities
is low.

Section 6.5.2           Subsidence and Karst Terrain

          A section of the Project will cross an area mapped as containing carbonate bedrock from
MP 68.98 to MP 70.95 (USGS, 2020).

Section 6.5.4           Flash Flooding

          Zone A is crossed by 15.36 miles of the Project, while Zone AE (including the floodway)
is crossed by 2.85 miles of the Project. Zone X (shaded) is crossed by 0.96 mile of the Project
(FEMA, 2026).

Section 7.3             Existing Soil Resources

          Modifications to the Project workspace have increased the number of soil map units to
153 units directly impacted by Project construction activities; however, no new soil series have
been identified within the Project workspace (Natural Resources Conservation Service, 2026).

Sections 7.5.4          Prime Farmland

          Approximately 1,122.93 acres (approximately 37 percent) of soil map units within the
Project area are classified as prime farmland. Of these, 1,096.55 acres of prime farmland are
associated with construction activities for the Texas Gateway Pipeline, while a total of 18.76 acres


                                                  16
 of prime farmland will be permanently impacted by operation of the Carthage Junction CS,
Magasco CS, Transco Delivery Meter Station, DWPL Line 200 Delivery Meter Station, Sempra
Delivery Meter Station, and other various aboveground appurtenant facilities.

       Approximately 8.19 acres and 316.22 acres of prime farmland (including farmland of
statewide importance and prime farmland if drained) impacted by the Project are characterized
as active agricultural and managed forested production, respectively. Impacts to these areas are
largely temporary in nature, with permanent impacts primarily associated with maintenance of
permanent right-of-way for the Texas Gateway Pipeline or the new aboveground facilities and
their associated access roads. The permanent easement within managed forest will not be
allowed to return to pre-existing use, as the easement will be maintained in an herbaceous state
to allow for aerial surveys and to ensure the integrity of the pipe is not compromised by tree roots.
In addition, approximately 0.22 acre of prime farmland characterized as managed forests will be
permanently converted to industrial use.


RESOURCE REPORT 8
Section 8.2.3          Construction and Operation Access

       A total of 105 access roads, requiring 285.25 acres, will be utilized for the Project
construction activities.   Of these access roads, 90 are TARs for use of the Project during
construction. A total of 15 permanent access roads will be utilized for permanent access to Project
components and will require a total of 26.44 acres during operation of the Project.

Section 8.3.2          Existing Residences and Buildings

       A total of five residences are located within 25 feet of the Project workspaces, and site-
specific residential construction drawings for those locations are provided as Appendix 8G.

Section 8.4.1          Public Land

Sabine National Forest / Moore Plantation Wildlife Management Area

       Although the Project is located within the proclaimed boundary of the Sabine National
Forest from MP 72.73 to MP 77.70 within Sabine County, Texas (USFS, 2026a, 2026b), the
Project will only cross land owned by the USFS at five distinct locations as detailed in Table 8.4-
1. Additionally, the Project workspace is within 0.25 mile of the Sabine National Forest from
MP 41.79 to MP 42.66, with the closest distance (0.08 mile) occurring at MP 42.40.




                                                 17
 El Camino Real de los Tejas Historic Trail

       The Project directly crosses the El Camino Real de los Tejas National Historic Trail from
approximately MP 46.97 to MP 47.01 as the trail follows Texas State Highway 21
(NPS, 2026b, 2026c).

Section 8.4.3          Natural, Recreational, or Scenic Areas

       The Project will cross the Sabine River at MP 120.38, which is listed on the NPS
Nationwide Rivers Inventory (NPS, 2026a). However, direct impacts to the Sabine River will be
avoided by utilizing the HDD crossing method.

       The Project will cross two state-designated scenic rivers: Beckwith Creek at MP 136.24
and MP 136.30 and Hickory Branch at MP 147.05 and MP 147.22 in Beauregard Parish,
Louisiana (LDWF, 2026a, 2026b).

       However, the Project crosses the Trail Between Lakes at MP 75.47, approximately 25 feet
east from the West Trailhead (Google Earth, 2026).

       The portion of U.S. Highway 96 crossing the Sabine National Forest is considered an
eligible Texas Scenic Byway and comes within 0.25 mile of the Project from MP 74.14 to MP 76.81
(Texas Department of Transportation, 2026).
